name: Education institution governance and administration
one_line: The institution's own side of running itself as an academic body: governing-instrument and committee business, academic regulations, programme approval and assessment-board records, registry and award operations, institution-authored quality self-evaluation, and statutory institutional returns. It is not activated by a university, college, or school name, by an academic-sounding topic, by an .edu-style domain, or by holding a document an institution issued. It differs from the Government default template by requiring an academic-cycle administrative anchor — academic year, programme or module code, cohort, assessment board, conferral round, or collection round — held on the producing institution's own side, and by carrying a mass named-student privacy posture that the proceeding-shaped default does not describe.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: these are template-activation signals, not licences to write facts. The Government schema declares no field rows under PR-6, so nothing here mints a school, programme, cohort, committee, or academic-year fact. Every accepted signal must show the corpus holder as the institution administering ITSELF, not as a student, an employee, a district or authority above it, an accrediting body reviewing it, or a reader.

a governing-instrument document — charter, statutes, ordinances, instrument and articles of government, or academic regulations — carrying numbered articles or regulations, a scheme of delegation or reservation of powers, a named governing body of the institution in whose header it sits, and an approving-committee and effective-date block; a generic employee handbook with the same furniture does not qualify

a two-tier academic governance pack in which a governing board or council paper set and a senate or academic board paper set carry the same institution block, a committee and meeting reference, numbered papers, attendance and apologies, a reserved-business or confidential-items section, and a minute or resolution; the two-body split (corporate governance separate from academic authority) is the discriminating structure

a programme approval or validation dossier repeating one programme identifier across a programme specification with credit values and learning outcomes, a module or unit list with module codes, a validation or approval panel report with conditions and recommendations, and a periodic-review or revalidation date

an assessment or examination board record combining a board minute, a ratified results or classification schedule keyed by module code and cohort, an external examiner report, and the institution's formal response to that report; the external-examiner-plus-response pair is the structure that distinguishes it from any one teacher's grading

a registry operations record keyed by academic year and programme — enrolment or registration register, census-date headcount return, programme transfer, interruption, withdrawal or reinstatement records, progression decisions, and award and conferral lists — produced by the institution about its own registered students

a statutory or funder institutional data return produced by the institution about itself, carrying a collection-round or reporting-year identifier, an institution identifier, a submission or validation report with error and query rows, and a sign-off block; the same statistics downloaded as a published table are reading material

an institution-authored quality self-evaluation or accreditation submission — self-study or self-evaluation document, standards-to-evidence mapping, evidence index, action or enhancement plan, review-visit schedule, and the institution's response to findings; authorship and custody must sit with the reviewed institution, not the reviewer

an academic policy or regulation set with version, approving-committee, review-date and applicability slots — assessment and progression regulations, academic misconduct procedure, admissions policy, appeals and complaints procedure, student protection or continuity plan — issued under the institution's own governing instrument

an institutional archive, student-records-system export, or backup manifest whose member paths repeatedly encode one academic year plus a programme, module, cohort, committee, or conferral round, and whose system or custodian metadata identifies the institution's registry, governance, or quality office; manifests are inspected without unpacking

an institutional email or calendar record whose structured sender, recipient, organizer, attendee, subject, attachment or event slots tie it to an already evidenced governance, registry, assessment-board, validation, return, or review workflow; an institutional mail domain alone never fires
needs_llm: deciding whether the institution is a publicly constituted body at all — a state university, a further-education corporation, or a maintained school sits inside the Government world, while an independent school, a private college, or a charitable university foundation may not; where public status cannot be evidenced the classifier must abstain and route to nonprofit or business_operations rather than assume, and this is the node's principal unresolved question

separating the institution's own side from the tier above it — a district, board, ministry, or local education authority administering many institutions — when both hold admissions data, statutory returns, funding allocations, and inspection correspondence with identical headings

separating the institution's own side from the reviewer's side when the same self-evaluation, evidence index, standards mapping, and visit schedule exist in both the accreditor's received-submissions pile and the institution's authoring folder

distinguishing an academic-governance paper from a generic organisational board pack when the agenda item is estates, audit, pay, or investment and nothing academic appears on the page; the surrounding pack, the governing instrument it cites, and the committee's terms of reference must supply the anchor

recognizing an unlabelled prose paper — a provost's discussion note, an unsigned options paper on programme closure, a draft regulation change — as institution-side governance work rather than a scholarly article about higher-education policy

deciding whether a cohort spreadsheet of marks is registry or assessment-board evidence held institutionally, or one instructor's private gradebook for one module, when both carry student names, module codes, and numeric columns
deciding whether an academic-year token, a programme title, or a module code in a filename reflects institution-side administration or merely the subject matter of a student's or reader's own file
never_alone: a university, college, school, faculty, campus, or academy name, crest, letterhead, seal, footer, PDF producer string, or metadata author; the design already refuses this shape, listing a “public school” among entities that may be issuer, counterparty, subject, employer, cited authority, research venue, or service provider
an institutional email domain, student-portal URL, or virtual-learning-environment link
the words university, campus, faculty, dean, provost, chancellor, registrar, senate, academic board, semester, syllabus, credits, or instructor; academic vocabulary is topic, not custody
an academic-year-shaped token such as 2025/26 or 2025-2026, a bare four-digit year, a term name, or an intake month
a course- or module-code-shaped token on its own; it needs institution-side administrative context, and even with academic context it evidences a course, not the governance of an institution

a student's own transcript, enrolment confirmation, results letter, degree certificate, tuition invoice, or student-card scan; the individual's education record belongs to the person's own academic, identity, finance, or Protected Records holdings even though a registry issued it

a downloaded prospectus, course catalogue, published inspection or accreditation report, league table, annual report, or higher-education policy paper held for reading; publication by an institution is not institution-side custody
one instructor's course pack, lecture deck, reading list, or single-module gradebook; teaching one course is not administering the institution
an employment contract, payslip, appraisal, or job advertisement bearing an institution's name; an institution as employer is not this template
a research grant application, ethics submission, or paper written at an institution; a research venue is not an administered institution
a file extension or source_type alone; the design says to “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a parent folder named University, School, College, Admin, Registry, Governance, Committee, or Academic Year alone
a shared download session or browser batch; “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
missing EXIF or dense OCR as proof that an image is a student-records-system screenshot; “the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot”

proposed_context_terms: the design floor for academic context is unchanged: syllabus, lecture, credits, instructor, semester. These are the institution-side administrative terms this template observes in real fixtures and proposes for R2's consideration; they are proposals, not design text.
governing instrument: statutes, ordinances, instrument of government, articles of government, scheme of delegation, reservation of powers, terms of reference
governance bodies: governing body, board of governors, council, senate, academic board, court, corporation, register of interests, reserved business
academic quality: programme specification, validation, revalidation, periodic review, learning outcomes, credit value, external examiner, self-evaluation, enhancement plan, condition of approval
registry operations: enrolment, registration, matriculation, census date, cohort, progression, interruption, withdrawal, conferral, award, academic transcript of record, student record system
institutional reporting: statutory return, collection round, data quality report, submission validation, institution identifier, reporting year
work_types: governing instrument and constitutional document — charter, statutes, ordinances, articles or instrument of government, scheme of delegation, committee terms of reference
governing body and academic body business — notice, agenda, numbered papers, pack, minute, resolution, action log, register of interests, effectiveness review
academic regulation and policy — assessment and progression regulations, academic misconduct procedure, admissions policy, appeals and complaints procedure, student protection or continuity plan
programme lifecycle — proposal, business case, programme specification, module descriptors, validation panel report, conditions, revalidation, suspension or closure and teach-out plan
assessment governance — assessment board minute, ratified results and classification schedule, moderation record, external examiner appointment, report and institutional response

registry operations — enrolment and registration register, census headcount, transfer, interruption and withdrawal record, progression decision, award and conferral list, certificate and transcript production record
admissions administration on the institution's side — cycle plan, offer-making and confirmation records, entry-requirement schedules, clearing and appeals against admission decisions
institutional reporting — statutory and funder data returns, validation and error reports, institutional performance and effectiveness reports, annual monitoring and enhancement reports
quality assurance on the reviewed side — self-evaluation or self-study, standards-to-evidence mapping, evidence index, review-visit logistics, findings response, condition-closure evidence
student-body and complaints administration — student charter, student-representation records, academic appeals, complaints and misconduct case administration held by the institution
institutional records management — retention schedule, records survey, archive accession, data-protection register entries for student and staff records
grouping_reasons: one governance cycle of one named body, linking notice, agenda, numbered papers, minute, resolutions, and action log by an exact committee-and-meeting reference; sparse members such as an unlabelled appendix join without acquiring a body, meeting, or date fact

one programme's approval lifecycle, linking proposal, specification, module descriptors, panel report, conditions, condition-closure evidence, annual monitoring, and revalidation by an exact programme identifier

one assessment board's cohort packet, linking board minute, ratified schedule, moderation record, external examiner report, and institutional response by an exact board-and-session reference; membership never copies a classification, mark, or student fact onto a member

one statutory return round, linking instrument or specification, extracted data, validation and error reports, resubmission, and sign-off by an exact collection-round identifier; the published output derived from it retains a different access boundary from the submitted record

one quality review episode, linking self-evaluation, evidence index, mapping, visit schedule, findings, and response by an exact review reference; the reviewer's own decision letter may sit in the same episode without making this corpus the reviewer's
one institutional export or archive manifest, kept shallow until access boundaries inside it are known, and never unpacked merely to strengthen recognition
duplicate and version families remain universal relationships; successive drafts of a regulation, specification, or policy do not acquire new facts from their neighbourhood

no group is a valid outcome for a standalone certificate, notice, published report, or confirmation; “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

template.why: Empty by contract: PR-6 leaves the Government schema fieldless and a template cannot branch on undeclared fields. The world nevertheless has a clear latent order, recorded here as prose for later adjudication rather than serialized: the administering institution, then the governing function or bounded academic object (governing body and committee, programme, assessment board, return round, or review episode), then the academic year or cycle, then work type. Named students and named staff must never become an organizing dimension, because a visible branch label can disclose an individual's education or disciplinary record. Time is not first: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” The academic year is a strong secondary cycle here but putting it first would split one programme's validation-to-revalidation record and one committee's continuous business across calendar folders. Any later order remains editable because “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The same admissions data, statutory returns, funding allocations, staffing records and inspection correspondence occur on both sides. The deciding evidence is the administrative tier: a district, board, ministry or local education authority administering many institutions it does not itself teach in, versus one institution administering itself under its own governing instrument. Same fixture both ways — an enrolment census by programme and mode: held by the district office as one school's row inside a multi-school aggregation it belongs to that row; produced by the institution's own registry about its own registered students it belongs here.

Self-evaluation documents, standards-to-evidence mappings, evidence indexes, visit schedules and findings responses exist identically on both sides. The deciding evidence is authorship and custody. Same fixture both ways — the self-evaluation document: authored and held by the reviewed institution's quality office it belongs here; received into a reviewing body's case inbox with a review reference, reviewer annotations and a panel worksheet it belongs to the accreditation row. Neither side may infer an accreditation outcome.

Notices, agendas, numbered papers, packs, minutes, resolutions and registers of interests are the same furniture in both worlds. The deciding evidence is the governing instrument and the two-tier academic split. Same fixture both ways — a governing-body minute: if its authority derives from an institution's statutes or instrument of government and an academic body (senate or academic board) holds separate academic authority, it belongs here; if it is a company or unit board operating under corporate articles with no academic authority tier, it belongs to board-governance. A university's audit-committee minute discussing only investments and estates is the hardest case and should abstain to Review Later rather than guess.

Governing documents, trustee or board business, policies, annual reporting and regulator correspondence overlap almost completely for an independent school, a charitable university foundation or a private college. The deciding evidence is public constitution. Same fixture both ways — a set of statutes with a scheme of delegation: if the institution is independently evidenced as a publicly constituted body it belongs here; if it is a charity, trust or private company running an educational institution, or if public status cannot be evidenced at all, it belongs to nonprofit governance. This template abstains rather than assuming, and NJ-1 records that the abstention may be wide.

Cohort spreadsheets with student names, module codes and mark columns occur on both sides. The deciding evidence is institutional apparatus versus one course. Same fixture both ways — a marks spreadsheet: with a board-and-session reference, moderation sheet, external examiner report and ratification it belongs here; as one instructor's working gradebook for one module with no board apparatus it belongs to academic.teaching, where school, term, subject and instructor are legal facts and none of them may be minted here.

Literally the same transcript bytes may sit in a registry's production record and in the graduate's own folder. The deciding evidence is holder role. Same fixture both ways — an official transcript with a seal and verification code: held by the named person alongside their identity and application material it belongs to transcripts-credentials; held inside a registry's conferral, reissue or verification workflow keyed by an award round it belongs here. Registrar language and a seal alone decide nothing.

falls_through_to.when: registry, assessment, misconduct, appeals, admissions or return material carrying identified students or staff has no safe accepted group, including cohort spreadsheets, conferral lists, case files and unopened records-system exports
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a readable standalone institutional document — a consolidated statutes copy, a policy issue, a published notice or a certificate — has durable value but no evidenced governance, programme, board, return or review workflow
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: prospectuses, published inspection or accreditation reports, sector policy papers, league tables and other institutions' governance documents are held for reading or study rather than as this institution's own administration
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: a document is plainly institutional administration but the tier, the reviewer-versus-reviewed side, or the institution's public constitution cannot be settled safely — including an unlabelled options paper and a university audit-committee pack with no academic content
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: an encrypted registry archive, a student-records database file, a damaged export or an unknown binary yields nothing beyond metadata
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

sensitivity_why: The design names the material directly: the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” This template's registry side is the institutional aggregation of exactly those educational records — a single ratified results sheet, conferral list, census extract or records-system export can carry an entire cohort of identified people with marks, classifications, progression outcomes, fee status, mitigating circumstances or disciplinary findings, and school-level cohorts may be minors. Governance packs add reserved business, staff disciplinary and pay items, and pre-decisional closure proposals. That is why the default posture is protective even though statutes, policies and published reports are low-risk bytes on their own: “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector,” and “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” No named student or staff member may become a folder level or a display label.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH (NJ-1): the roster places this row on the Government schema, but that schema requires an evidenced public authority, while a large share of the world named in the one_line_hint — independent schools, private colleges, charitable university foundations — is not one. This pass narrows the row to publicly constituted institutions and abstains to nonprofit or business_operations otherwise. The alternatives are: (a) keep the narrowing and accept that private-institution governance is covered only by nonprofit.governance and business_operations.board-governance; (b) reassign the row to a schema that does not presuppose public status; (c) split it into a public and an independent sibling. R1c should decide before any field vocabulary is adjudicated. NJ-2: decide whether a bounded academic-cycle anchor (academic year plus a programme, board, return round or committee reference) may ever be a stored fact and a destination level, given that its display label is safe while a student identifier's is not.
